copy.title: Comp line
copy.body: TV Girl meets Hope Sandoval & The Warm Inventions. Drum-machine and tape-warped melodic dream pop with the ambient, introspective pull of a small-town exit song. Fans of both share a taste for love, intimacy and relationships.
copy.hint: The one-line "X meets Y" that opens every pitch.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Playlist & press pitch
copy.body: Glass Hours is hazy, synth-washed dream pop about leaving a small town, built on drum machines and tape-warped guitars. It sits near TV Girl for melody and sample-minded texture, and near Hope Sandoval & The Warm Inventions for ambient, introspective mood. Listeners of Tanukichan and Weyes Blood will find the same pull between warmth and distance, and the Japanese Breakfast, Beach House, Mazzy Star and Cocteau Twins audience is where the record fits best. Suited to dream pop and late-night playlists, and to press that covers Jay Som and Lush.
copy.hint: The "sounds like / for fans of" pitch for editors, blogs and promoters.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience around Japanese Breakfast, Beach House, Mazzy Star and Cocteau Twins over-indexes at 35–44 (+0.30) and under-indexes at 45–54 (-0.46). Gender is near even. Its taste descriptors are dream pop, shoegaze, lo-fi, experimental and psychedelic. It also loves Lost in Translation, Frances Ha and Eighth Grade, listens to Song Exploder and Love and Radio, and shops at Urban Outfitters, Anthropologie and Madewell. Markets flagged: Missoula as a hidden gem, plus Seattle, Madison, El Paso, Portland and Santa Fe as emerging. This is aggregate taste, not a forecast.

copy.body:

• Fans of Hope Sandoval & The Warm Inventions: slow, hazy and introspective, with tape-warped guitars that drift rather than push.
• Fans of Tanukichan: bedroom-scale dream pop, synth-washed and intimate, made for headphones.

kit.headline: TV Girl meets Hope Sandoval & The Warm Inventions is where Glass Hours sits: sample-minded dream pop with the slow, introspective drift of Japanese Breakfast, Beach House, Mazzy Star and Cocteau Twins listeners.
kit.summary: Glass Hours sits in dream pop, close to the indie-to-mid-list artists the Japanese Breakfast, Beach House, Mazzy Star and Cocteau Twins audience already follows. Lead with TV Girl and Hope Sandoval & The Warm Inventions, then use Tanukichan as the niche, closest-fit comp. The audience skews 35–44 and shows no gender tilt, and it overlaps with podcast, film and lifestyle-brand taste, so editorial and channel pitches can go beyond music press.
